goal: Operator order 2026-11-01: understand the recent phases FIRST, then decide how to backtest. Phase 1 (design set, look freely): walk the recent BTC 15m/1h from the 60k low through the 87k top to now; mark every H1, L1, held retest, L1 sweep, H1 take-out and the drop after, with time of day (US session), OI change during the retest, WaveTrend/RSI divergence at H1 and the nearest volume node; a dated table plus chart screenshots. Phase 2: from what Phase 1 shows, write the step definitions and the trade legs and freeze them (OURS, operator confirms on >= 3 of his own charts, PRE_REG_TEMPLATE 0g). Phase 3: test the frozen rules on DEV 2022-04..2024-06 split by up/down regime; the recent window is seen and never counts as the test.
note: Operator 2026-11-01 HEDGE framing: the legs are not each a trade to judge alone. Core = the position on the main idea (e.g. short from H1 for the final drop); hedge = a temporary opposite position on the leg against it (e.g. long into the held-retest / H1 take-out), closed when that leg plays out, because the reversal back to the core idea is expected. Score the BOOK, not the legs: core alone vs core + hedge on net P&L after fees.py fees on every leg, max adverse excursion, and core stop-outs avoided. A hedge leg with gross about 0 (C26 arm A) can still pay if it lets the core survive the squeeze; it is a NO if the extra fees exceed the drawdown it saves. Execution note for Phase 2: a same-venue hedge in one-way mode just nets the position (needs hedge mode, a second venue, or options); testnet only.
title: C26 roadmap as a state machine: high H1 -> low L1 -> held retest of H1 (OI build) -> L1 sweep -> H1 take-out -> drop; per-step odds by regime (up/down), maker-entry legs at volume nodes, recent-regime readout
